newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ranariddh should be part of Cambodia polls - Manila.
newsitem.headline: Ranariddh should be part of Cambodia polls - Manila.

text.p: Cambodia's rulers should allow ousted first prime minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh to take part in next May's general elections, Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said on Wednesday.
Siazon, chairman of the standing committee of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), also said ASEAN was prepared to assist Cambodia in holding the polls.
He gave no specific details of any proposals.
ASEAN was to have accepted Cambodia as a new member last month but deferred its membership after Ranariddh was ousted by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
Siazon was a member of an ASEAN panel involved in mediation efforts to restore stability in Cambodia.

"What is important for us is to ensure that on the ground, you have an administration that is effectively running the day to day affairs of Cambodia so that the Khmer (Cambodian) people will not suffer, and two, that you have an administration that can actually implement the holding of elections in May," Siazon told reporters.
Another factor, he said, is that "Prince Ranariddh will at a given point in time be able to participate in the elections", Siazon added.
A new first prime minister has been sworn in and a warrant issued for Ranariddh's arrest on charges of weapons smuggling. Ranariddh fled the country early last month.
Hun Sen had previously ruled with Ranariddh in an uneasy coalition government that took power after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
The nine-member ASEAN comprises Brunei, Burma, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
